why: Most of the builder brief states the bar without handing over the checker's methods. It doesn't use the verifier's fixtures (a.jsonl, b.jsonl, bad.jsonl), its command lines or its PASS/FAIL wording. Telling the builder to run `npm test`, wait for the `test` workflow and write node:test tests is allowed. One place breaks the criterion. Step 2 says "`git diff` of that file against the base must be empty", which hands the builder a probe plus a pass condition. Verifier Check 4 uses that same probe: `git diff <merge-base>..HEAD -- packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js`. No expect line or issue proof names git diff, so the exception for allowed commands doesn't cover it. Because the builder gets a probe that also appears in the verifier brief, the criterion fails.
